pick.reason: The headline is the image. It reads in two seconds at thumbnail size on both sizes, follows Ferro's white, black and one-red rule exactly, and is closest to the bar with the fewest notes.
pick.lost: 1 the landscape headline is small at about 56px, and the grey right half and the lower white column are left over, not shaped; 2 the black field breaks the brand's first rule (white background, black type) and splits the canvas into two unrelated blocks
notes: ig-post: the supporting line goes from 31px to 39px (on scale), line height 1.3, and its gap below the headline goes from about 48px to 64px. This shrinks the empty band between the supporting line and the mark from about 450px (a third of the canvas, a composition fault in the standard's "Owns the whole canvas" rule) to about 400px.

linkedin: the content column's left edge moves from 48px to 72px so it meets the brief's 6% safe zone on the long side and matches the ig-post column. The top margin stays at 40px. Check that "November 8." still ends inside 1128px.
Both sizes: the mark stays at 16px muted #737373, left-aligned on the same column as the headline, with its baseline on the bottom safe line (589px on linkedin, 1215px on ig-post).
Both sizes: the headline tracking is -0.02em and the line height is 1.0. Keep red on "November 8" only and the full stop in foreground #0a0a0a, as it is now.

spacing: on ig-post, set the gap between "November 8." and the supporting line to 80px (currently about 100px), so the headline and the supporting line read as one group. On linkedin, keep the gaps as they are.

composition: on ig-post, take the supporting line from 39px to 49px at line height 1.3, keeping the mark at 16px with its baseline on 1215px. This cuts the empty band from about 370px to under 300px, so the type block carries the canvas instead of leaving the air over.

originality: on both sizes, shift the headline 4px left so the round "O", "S" and "N" align optically with the "B" stem of the supporting line and the "f" of the mark. That machined edge is what makes this Ferro's card and not a template's.
polish: On linkedin, hold the 40px top margin, but check that the cap top of "Open" sits at 72px to match the left edge, so the corner reads square.
